input.prompt: A square matte-black circuit board seen perfectly head-on from directly above, flat, no perspective, filling the whole frame edge to edge. Four big identical square chip sockets nearly fill the board in a 2 by 2 grid: each socket is 43% of the board's width, and the gaps between them are narrow, only 5% of the board's width. Each socket is an empty window of deep glossy black glass inside a thin raised brushed-steel frame with a ring of tiny silver solder pads. Short bright brushed-silver traces bridge the narrow gaps between the sockets clockwise: top-left to top-right, top-right down to bottom-right, bottom-right to bottom-left, bottom-left back up to top-left, forming a loop. Four small silver mounting holes in the board's corners. Hand-painted American comic book illustration of a real physical object, like a premium graphic-novel panel: modelled with one soft warm-white key light from the upper left and deep shadows, confident black ink contour lines, fine Ben-Day halftone dots only inside the darkest shadows, set in a pure black void with nothing else in it. Materials: matte black solder mask with a fine grain, dark graphite traces barely visible, brushed silver-steel metal. Strictly no green anywhere, no red, no blue, no purple, no coloured lights, no rim lights, no glow, no lens flare. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no symbols, no markings, no labels anywhere.
